key_insight: KaiNinja extends a native single-shot 3D generator from whole objects to part-level assets by replacing the original O-Voxel with a dual-volume representation that can model touching part interfaces.
engineering_relevance: This makes part-aware 3D generation faster and more practical for editing, rigging, and simulation than post-hoc segmentation pipelines.
method: Builds on TRELLIS.2’s native 3D generation pipeline.
Uses a dual-volume O-Voxel form to represent adjacent parts without losing the interface between them.
Trains without masks or an external segmenter, using mixed data including CAD and agent-authored part assets.
evidence_signal: The paper reports a 40% lower whole-object Chamfer distance and a 16% higher strict part F-score versus other part-generation approaches.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and diversity of part-level training data, so the dual-volume pipeline may be limited by dataset coverage and scaling complexity.
paper_title: Kaininja: Extending Native 3D Generators to the Part Level
